newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Grains-China buys 100,000T S.American soymeal.
newsitem.headline: China Grains-China buys 100,000T S.American soymeal.

text.p: Hong Kong grains traders confirmed on Thursday that China bought 100,000 tonnes of South American soymeal for delivery at the end of May or beginning of June to a south China port but could not agree on the prices.
"That's a confirmed trade," said one trader.
The price of the deal was likely at $304-305 per tonne, C&F China, but some traders said it could have been slightly higher.
No further deals were heard in the pipeline on Thursday.
The price of domestic meal was stable, supply was abundant and there were few signs to indicate meal would rise over the next two weeks, they said.
Domestic meal in south China was heard around 2,900 yuan ($349) per tonne, compared with imported meal which was at about 2,800 yuan per tonne.
In the northern city of Dalian, domestic meal was at 2,770 yuan per tonne and in Shandong province it was priced at 2,800 yuan per tonne, sources said.
"We expect prices to remain stable," said one grains trader.
Soybean supplies in China were also relatively healthy, with beans in Shandong heard at 3,200 yuan per tonne, up 50 to 100 yuan per tonne compared to last month, a source said.
Soybean stocks in Heilongjiang were swollen, one trader said.
"The problem is they don't have rail (carriages) to ship soybeans to the south," he said.
Shenyang Railway Administration had transported 3.6 million tonnes of grain from reserves in northeastern China to southern regions, the Economic Information Daily said on Tuesday.
Corn was heard at 1,120 yuan per tonne in Dalian.
